top_news.title: Bounded Personas Match Retrieval on Classification but Not Regression for a Frozen Agent
top_news.dek: Distilled personas match retrieval-based methods for classification tasks but underperform in regression for frozen language agents.
top_news.brief: Researchers compared retrieval-based history management against distilled natural-language personas. While distillation offers lower latency and query independence, it struggles to maintain accuracy in regression tasks compared to retrieval, which pulls specific past interactions into the prompt.
top_news.image_alt: Comparison chart showing performance gap between retrieval and distillation methods

top_news.title: Run agent-driven Amazon SageMaker HyperPod operations with InstantStart
top_news.dek: AWS introduced HyperPod InstantStart, an open-source control plane for agent-driven SageMaker HyperPod operations.
top_news.brief: HyperPod InstantStart integrates Amazon EKS orchestration with SageMaker HyperPod to automate complex infrastructure tasks. It provides a unified interface for AI agents to manage cluster bootstrapping, capacity provisioning, training, and inference, reducing operational friction in multi-step foundation model workflows.

top_news.title: Once popular for attacking AI, ASCII smuggling is embraced by spammers
top_news.dek: ASCII smuggling, once used for adversarial AI attacks, is now being widely adopted by spammers to bypass content filters.
top_news.brief: Spammers are increasingly utilizing ASCII smuggling—a technique involving invisible Unicode characters—to evade automated detection systems. While previously identified as a vector for adversarial AI attacks, the method is now seeing broader deployment in spam campaigns to obfuscate malicious content from traditional security filters.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of hidden text layers in digital communication.

top_news.title: Google AI Mode shows same products 21.6% more expensive than traditional search
top_news.dek: A 23-day study of 2 million listings found that Google AI Mode results feature products 21.6% more expensive than traditional search.
top_news.brief: Researchers comparing Google AI Mode against traditional search results found a consistent price discrepancy. When the same product appeared in both interfaces, the AI-generated recommendations were on average 21.6% more expensive, suggesting potential biases in how AI models prioritize or select commercial listings.
top_news.image_alt: Comparison chart showing price differences between AI search and traditional search.

top_news.title: Anthropic: Formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem
top_news.dek: Anthropic has released a complete, computer-checked proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem generated largely autonomously by Claude.
top_news.brief: Claude successfully formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem in the Lean programming language over an 11-day period. This achievement demonstrates the growing capability of LLMs to handle complex, multi-step formal mathematical reasoning, marking a significant milestone for AI-assisted research mathematics.
top_news.image_alt: Mathematical notation and code representing the formal proof.

primary.title: Counterexamples as Feedback for Agent Self-Correction
primary.summary: Single-turn code-generation metrics understate a central property of deployed agents: whether they can repair a wrong artifact after receiving concrete feedback. An agent proposes a regex, a deterministic oracle checks it under full-match semantics, and compact false-positive or false-negative witnesses guide the next turn.
